chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Ribāṭ, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A boy is ten years old, and his father marries him off while he is still young. Is his divorce valid while he is the son of ten years?

He said: As for the marriage, it is valid. But as for his divorce, his wife should be withheld for him until he reaches maturity, and it is ascertained that he had indeed divorced. If he acknowledges that and ratifies it, then it is one irrevocable divorce, and he is a suitor among the suitors. But if he denies that and refuses to ratify it, then she is his wife.

I said: What if she dies or he dies? He said: The inheritance is to be withheld until whichever of the two remains reaches maturity. Then he is made to swear by Allah that nothing called him to take the inheritance except acceptance of the marriage, and the inheritance is handed over to him.

key_terms.التَّزْوِيجُ: marriage contract being concluded for the minor
key_terms.الرِّضَا بِالنِّكَاحِ: acceptance and approval of the marriage
key_terms.خَاطِبٌ مِنَ الْخُطَّابِ: a suitor among other suitors after separation

ai.seo_question: Is the marriage and divorce of a ten-year-old boy valid in Shia fiqh, and what happens to inheritance if one spouse dies before maturity?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on a minor boy married by his father: the marriage is valid, but a divorce issued by the child is not immediately effective until he reaches maturity and confirms it. It also explains the inheritance ruling if one spouse dies before maturity, requiring the surviving minor to reach maturity and swear that claiming the inheritance is based on accepting the marriage.
